runs.question: Query the first-seen block arrival times for mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026 (UTC).
runs.answer:
[Turn 1 | session=ses_0ece1f8f6ffebaKuvzTDCPJW2F] Query the first-seen block arrival times for mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026 (UTC).
Here are the first-seen block arrival times for mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026. The query used `mainnet.fct_block_first_seen_by_node`, taking the minimum `seen_slot_start_diff` (ms from slot start) per slot.

**Summary for 20 June 2026:**
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total blocks | 7,180 |
| Avg first-seen | 1,710 ms |
| Min first-seen | 141 ms |
| Max first-seen | 5,249 ms |
| P50 (median) | 1,453 ms |
| P95 | 3,126 ms |
| P99 | 3,314 ms |

The data shows per-slot first-seen times across the full UTC day. Most blocks are first seen within ~1.5s of the slot start, with P95 around 3.1s. There were 7,180 blocks observed for that day (covering slots ~14590400 through ~14597998).

The full per-slot result (7,180 rows) was too large to display inline but was saved. You can drill into specific slot ranges or time windows with a refined query.

[Turn 2 | session=ses_0ece1f8f6ffebaKuvzTDCPJW2F] Plot the distribution of those arrival times as a chart.
The histogram chart is available at:

**URL:** `http://127.0.0.1:2480/api/v1/storage/files/f9dbda681a3a/d3e83098-3ec2-418b-bca6-3c59bf40c7e0/first_seen_distribution.png`

It shows the distribution of first-seen block arrival times (ms from slot start) for mainnet blocks on 20 June 2026 — most blocks arrive within ~2 seconds, with a long tail beyond 3 s.
